title: Purify water
summary: Make water of unknown quality safe to drink by boiling or with household bleach.
outline: Distillation for salt or chemical water [step]

cards.headline: Clear stream water can still make you sick
cards.body: Water from lakes, ponds, springs, and streams can carry germs you can't see. Treat any water you aren't sure about before drinking it, cooking with it, or brushing your teeth.

cards.headline: Cloudy water? Let it settle, then strain it
cards.body: Let dirt sink to the bottom, then pour the clearer water through a clean cloth, paper towel, or coffee filter. This only clears it. You still have to boil or disinfect it.

cards.headline: Boil water to make it safe
cards.body: Bring clear water to a rolling boil for at least 1 minute. At high altitude, boil for 3 minutes. Let it cool before drinking.

sources.title: CDC: Making water safe in an emergency

cards.deeper: Boiling kills the bacteria, viruses, and parasites that cause most waterborne illness. Agencies differ on where high altitude starts: EPA says above 5,000 feet, CDC says above 6,500 feet. Using 3 minutes anywhere in the mountains covers both. Boiling does not remove chemicals, salts, or heavy metals.

cards.headline: No way to boil? Use plain bleach
cards.body: Add 8 drops of plain, unscented 6% bleach per gallon. Double it if the water is cloudy, colored, or very cold. Stir and wait at least 30 minutes before drinking.

mistakes: Using scented, color-safe, or cleaner-added bleach
Drinking before the 30 minutes are up
Using a bottle that has sat open for over a year

cards.headline: Treated water should smell faintly of chlorine
cards.body: After 30 minutes, the water should smell slightly of chlorine. If it doesn't, add the same dose again and wait 15 more minutes. Too strong? Pour it between clean containers.

cards.headline: Only plain, unscented bleach can treat water
cards.body: Check the label for sodium hypochlorite and a disinfection use. Skip scented and color-safe bleach, and bleach with added cleaners. Fresh bottles work best because bleach weakens over time.

cards.headline: Iodine is a backup, not a first choice
cards.body: Boil or use bleach first. If iodine is all you have, add 5 drops of 2% tincture per quart, 10 if cloudy, and wait 30 minutes. Skip it if pregnant or with thyroid problems.

cards.headline: Boiling kills germs but not chemicals
cards.body: Boiling and bleach kill most germs. They don't remove fuel, salts, heavy metals, or most chemicals. If you think water has fuel or chemicals in it, find another source.

cards.headline: Boiled water tastes flat. Pour it back and forth.
cards.body: Pour boiled, cooled water between two clean containers a few times to put air back in. A pinch of salt per quart also helps.

cards.headline: After adding bleach, how long before you drink?
cards.body: Bleach needs time to work on germs.
